findings.title: Confusing dead-code logic in enableSqlExpressions makes the security gate fragile
findings.body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the inverted naming — `enabled` actually means 'feature flag is NOT set') and then has an `if enabled { return false }` followed by an unconditional `return false`. Both branches return `false`, so the function always disables SQL expressions regardless of the feature-flag state — which is presumably the intent (to patch the RCE/LFI vulnerability), but the code reads as if it is supposed to check the flag and enable the feature when set. This is highly confusing: a future maintainer looking at this code will likely 'fix' the apparent dead branch/unused logic, assuming it's a bug, and could inadvertently re-enable the vulnerable SQL-expression execution path. Given this function is the primary gate preventing exploitation of the CVE, it should be a single explicit `return false` with a clear comment explaining why SQL expressions are permanently disabled, not an inverted boolean with unreachable branches.

findings.title: No tests added/updated verifying SQL expressions are now blocked
findings.body: The PR introduces a security-critical change (fully disabling SQL expression execution via `enableSqlExpressions` and stubbing out the SQL engine) but does not add or update any tests in `pkg/expr` to assert that: (1) `ReadQuery` returns the 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error for `QueryTypeSQL` regardless of feature flag state, and (2) `SQLCommand.Execute`/`NewSQLCommand` fail safely now that `sql.TablesList`/`QueryFramesInto` always return errors. Without such tests, a future refactor could silently reintroduce the vulnerable code path (e.g., by 'fixing' the dead logic in `enableSqlExpressions`) without any test catching the regression.

findings.title: Leftover 'duckDB' variable name contradicts PR's stated goal to remove DuckDB references
findings.body: The PR description states the goal is to 'Remove reference to DuckDB', but `TablesList` still assigns `duckDB := NewInMemoryDB()`, keeping a DuckDB-specific variable name even though the underlying DuckDB dependency (`scottlepp/go-duck`) has been removed and replaced by the stub `DB` struct. This is a minor but visible inconsistency with the PR's own description and could confuse future readers into thinking a DuckDB engine is still in use.

findings.title: Stub error messages ('not implemented') obscure that the feature is intentionally and permanently disabled for security reasons
findings.body: All methods on the new stub `DB` type (`TablesList`, `RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`) return a generic `errors.New("not implemented")`. Combined with the feature-flag check that also always disables SQL expressions, this gives operators/support staff no indication that the feature was intentionally and permanently removed due to a security vulnerability (CVE-2024-9264) rather than simply unfinished. This can lead to confusing support tickets or well-meaning future attempts to 'finish implementing' the stub, inadvertently reopening the vulnerability if not accompanied by a code comment or clearer error message explaining the deliberate removal.
